issues.legal_issue: Parliament may impose a tax on gifts of land and buildings under its residuary legislative power when the tax is on the value of gifts rather than on ownership of the land and buildings.
material_facts: Parliament enacted a law imposing tax on gifts, including gifts of agricultural land, plantations, and buildings.
The challenged tax was calculated on the value of the total gifts made during a year above the exempted limit; the land and buildings were valued to measure the gifts.
The tax was challenged on the ground that the State List reserved legislative power over land and taxes on land and buildings to the States.
No Union List or Concurrent List entry specifically mentioned a gift tax.
issues.conclusion: The gift tax was not a tax on land and buildings as such, and no State List entry covered it; Parliament was therefore competent to enact the law under its residuary power.
issues.legal_principle: The Constitution separately enumerates legislative subjects and taxing powers, and a general subject-matter entry does not itself confer a power to impose a tax. Under Article 248 and Union List Entry 97, Parliament may legislate, including by imposing a tax, on a matter not enumerated in the Concurrent or State Lists. State List Entry 18 concerning land does not authorize an unenumerated tax. Entry 49 concerns a tax directly imposed by reason of general ownership of land and buildings. Applying the pith-and-substance approach to legislative entries, a tax measured by the value of gifts is a tax on the transfer of property by gift, even when the property includes land or buildings. The Court followed Sudhir Chandra Nawn v. Wealth Tax Officer and referred to State of Rajasthan v. S. Chawla on interpreting legislative entries; it also approved S. Dhandapani v. Addl. Gift Tax Officer, Shyam Sunder v. Gift Tax Officer, Jupadi Sesharatnam v. Gift Tax Officer, and Joseph v. Gift Tax Officer.

rule.if: legislative_competence_challenge and parliamentary_tax_law and gifts_of_land_or_buildings_taxed and tax_measured_by_total_gift_value and not tax_based_on_general_ownership and no_enumerated_entry_covers_gift_tax

predicates.legislative_competence_challenge: The proceeding challenges whether the national legislature had authority to enact the tax law.
predicates.parliamentary_tax_law: The national legislature enacted a law imposing the tax.
predicates.gifts_of_land_or_buildings_taxed: The tax was imposed on gifts that included land or buildings.
predicates.tax_measured_by_total_gift_value: The tax was calculated by reference to the value of gifts made, with land or buildings valued as part of those gifts.
predicates.tax_based_on_general_ownership: The tax was imposed directly because a person generally owned land or buildings.
predicates.no_enumerated_entry_covers_gift_tax: No specifically enumerated legislative or taxing subject covered the tax on gifts.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a parliamentary tax law taxing gifts of land or buildings by reference to total gift value, rather than general ownership, and no enumerated entry covers the gift tax, the national legislature has residuary competence to impose it.
